import pandas as pd
X = pd.DataFrame({
    "colour":   ["red", "blue", "red", "green", "blue", "green", "red", "blue"],
    "size_cm":  [10.0, 12.5, 9.0, 15.0, 11.0, 14.0, 10.5, 13.0],
    "weight_g": [120, 150, 110, 200, 140, 190, 125, 160],
})

Build a single `Pipeline` that one-hot encodes `colour`, standardises the two numeric columns, and fits a `LogisticRegression`. Fit it on `X, y`. Then call `predict_proba` on this one-row frame, which contains a colour never seen in training, and it must not raise: `{"colour": "purple", "size_cm": 12.0, "weight_g": 150}`. Give the complete runnable code and explain in two sentences why the unseen colour does not cause an error. Do not use any library beyond pandas and scikit-learn.

```python
import pandas as pd
X = pd.DataFrame({
    "colour":   ["red", "blue", "red", "green", "blue", "green", "red", "blue"],
    "size_cm":  [10.0, 12.5, 9.0, 15.0, 11.0, 14.0, 10.5, 13.0],

})
y = [0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1]
```

Build a single `Pipeline` that one-hot encodes `colour`, standardises the two numeric columns, and fits a `LogisticRegression`. Fit it on `X, y`. Then call `predict_proba` on this one-row frame, which contains a colour never seen in training, and it must not raise: `{"colour": "purple", "size_cm": 12.0, "weight_g": 150}`. Give the complete runnable code and explain in two sentences why the unseen colour does not cause an error. Do not use any library beyond pandas and scikit-learn.

content:
```python
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder, StandardScaler
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

X = pd.DataFrame({
    "colour":   ["red", "blue", "red", "green", "blue", "green", "red", "blue"],
    "size_cm":  [10.0, 12.5, 9.0, 15.0, 11.0, 14.0, 10.5, 13.0],
    "weight_g": [120, 150, 110, 200, 140, 190, 125, 160],
})
y = [0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1]

X_train = pd.DataFrame(X, columns=X.columns)
X_new = pd.DataFrame({"colour": ["purple"], "size_cm": [12.0], "weight_g": [150.0]})

pre = ColumnTransformer([
    ("num", StandardScaler(), ["size_cm", "weight_g"]),
    ("cat", OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore"), ["colour"]),
])
pipe = Pipeline([
    ("pre", pre),
    ("clf", LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000)),
])
pipe.fit(X_train, y)

print(pipe.predict_proba(X_new))
```

The unseen colour does not raise an error because `OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore")` drops columns for categories not present in the training set, so the pipeline always outputs the same number of columns and `LogisticRegression.predict_proba` can operate.
